common_core_vs_original_member_cores: The common midpoint ±0.25 Å metric core is not the full union of the four original member cores: their edge shifts are ±0.0025 Å. All four exact catalog markers and original core bounds remain explicit, and the full wavelength intervals of all four original cores lie within the fixed ±3 Å spectral context. Finite profile coverage is reported separately. Raw panels retain their original crop geometry separately from spectral core coverage. A common-window statistic does not separately classify each nearby feature.
conclusion: For each of the four fixed discovery references, all six other HD114386 epochs agree better in barycentric coordinates than in the fixed topocentric frame, in both the common group core and surrounding window. V2E2-0094/0096/0098/0110 all remain U. The central rounded structure, nearby secondary rise and wider pattern recur with retained amplitude and shape differences. These descriptive comparisons do not identify a line or physical origin, qualify a laser candidate, estimate significance or calibrate a null result.

fixed_geometry.center_rule: Midpoint of minimum/maximum original catalog centers 4303.785 and 4303.79 Angstrom, following existing joint-group convention; not a fitted peak.
fixed_geometry.common_core_basis: Fixed 0.5-Angstrom group comparison interval centered on midpoint. It is not the union or entire original core of any shifted member, and is not a measured physical linewidth.
fixed_geometry.grid: 601 centers from -3 to +3 Angstrom in 0.01 Angstrom steps; 51 common-core and 550 surrounding centers.
fixed_geometry.anchor_selection_rule: First original ACTION_QUEUE member 0094 fixes one common March 2022 topocentric group anchor. All four discovery products remain separate comparison references; no favorable-reference selection.
fixed_geometry.anchor_change_from_prior_phases: New target HD114386 with own seven 2022–2023 epochs, four references and first-queue March anchor. No HD112410 products, May 2025 reference, numeric anchor, seven-inside geometry or BERV span transfers.

joint_reference_dependence.interpretation: Four fixed references reuse the same seven observing profiles. Each reference has six other-epoch comparisons; 24 ordered nonself records per frame/region are not 24 independent epochs or detections. The six unordered discovery-reference pairs appear in both directions and repeat pair information; even the 18 distinct pairs share observations. Retain per-reference statistics and source/reference identities. Sixteen identical-product self rows and all same-exposure native/merged comparisons add no independent observing evidence.

current_topocentric_geometry: 3 of seven metadata-predicted group centers remain inside the fixed March-anchor ±0.25 Å topocentric core and 4 lie outside. These are predicted centers rather than fitted peaks or full finite-feature coverage. No epoch or discovery reference is recentered; a fixed-window comparison can include neighboring structure after a predicted center leaves the core. Frame statistics are descriptive, not calibrated origin tests.
historical_mapping_context: All four original order-19 contexts retain every historical mapping stage as true; later diagnostics and native/merged agreement do not establish physical origin.
historical_raw_context: All four records retain primary, secondary and adopted U for broad rounded native features, nearby shoulders/structure and weak diffuse trace-associated raw enhancement. Their four original order-19 contexts retain true global/local/baseline and later five-window mapping stages. Supported mapping and extraction agreement do not identify a physical origin or qualify a narrow source. Original raw panels, reviews and dispositions remain unchanged.

All four original order-19 contexts have true global/local/baseline and later five-window mapping diagnostics; do not transfer other-wavelength mapping discrepancies.
